use: The everyday word for your mobile phone.

example.ja: スマホ忘れちゃった。

examplePolite.romaji: Sumaho o wasurete shimaimashita.
examplePolite.ja: スマホを忘れてしまいました。
examplePolite.english: I've forgotten my phone.

notes: Short for sumaato fon. Keitai is the older word, still heard.

english: LINE (messaging app); a LINE message; line
use: Japan's main messaging app; rain suru means 'message someone on LINE'.

example.ja: あとでLINEするね。
example.english: I'll message you on LINE later.

examplePolite.romaji: Ato de rain shimasu ne.
examplePolite.ja: あとでLINEしますね。
examplePolite.english: I'll message you on LINE later.

notes: Also 'line' in general, like a limit: rain o koeru = cross the line.

example.romaji: Kono apuri, mechakucha benri da yo.
example.ja: このアプリ、めちゃくちゃ便利だよ。

examplePolite.romaji: Kono apuri, totemo benri desu yo.
examplePolite.ja: このアプリ、とても便利ですよ。
examplePolite.english: This app is really handy.

notes: Short for apurikeeshon. You 'put in' an app: apuri o ireru.

use: The 'Read' mark LINE shows once someone opens your message.

example.romaji: Kidoku ni natteru noni henji nai.
example.ja: 既読になってるのに返事ない。
example.english: It says read, but there's no reply.

examplePolite.romaji: Kidoku ni natte iru noni, henji ga arimasen.
examplePolite.ja: 既読になっているのに、返事がありません。
examplePolite.english: It shows as read, but there's no reply.

notes: Kidoku suruu = reading a message and not replying.

example.ja: それ、スクショして送って。
example.english: Screenshot that and send it to me.

examplePolite.romaji: Sore o sukusho shite okutte kudasai.
examplePolite.ja: それをスクショして送ってください。
examplePolite.english: Please take a screenshot of that and send it.

notes: Short for sukuriinshotto; sukusho suru = take a screenshot.

example.romaji: Dotchi mo ii kara, ryouhou kau.
example.ja: どっちもいいから、両方買う。
example.english: They're both nice, so I'll buy both.

examplePolite.romaji: Dochira mo ii no de, ryouhou kaimasu.
examplePolite.ja: どちらもいいので、両方買います。
examplePolite.english: They're both nice, so I'll take both.

notes: Only for two things; for three or more use zenbu.

use: Stresses that each person or thing is separate or different.

example.ja: みんなそれぞれ違うからね。

examplePolite.romaji: Minna sorezore chigaimasu kara ne.
examplePolite.ja: みんなそれぞれ違いますからね。
examplePolite.english: Everyone is different, after all.

use: Sounds a bit serious or written; in everyday talk zenbu is more usual.

example.romaji: Okane ga subete ja nai yo.
example.ja: お金が全てじゃないよ。

examplePolite.romaji: Okane ga subete ja arimasen yo.
examplePolite.ja: お金が全てじゃありませんよ。
examplePolite.english: Money isn't everything.

notes: Also works as an adverb: subete owatta = it's all done.

use: An emotional 'everything', often when it all goes wrong or you're fed up.

example.romaji: Mou nanimo kamo iya ni natta.
example.ja: もう何もかも嫌になった。

examplePolite.romaji: Mou nanimo kamo iya ni narimashita.
examplePolite.ja: もう何もかも嫌になりました。
examplePolite.english: I've had enough of everything.

notes: Not nanimo alone, which takes a negative and means 'nothing'.

use: Something seen as one whole; zentaiteki ni = overall, on the whole.

example.ja: 全体的にはよかったよ。

examplePolite.romaji: Zentaiteki ni wa yokatta desu.
examplePolite.ja: 全体的にはよかったです。
examplePolite.english: On the whole, it was good.

notes: Zenbu counts every item; zentai looks at the whole as one.

example.ja: 半分食べていいよ。

examplePolite.romaji: Hanbun tabete ii desu yo.
examplePolite.ja: 半分食べていいですよ。
examplePolite.english: Please, have half.

notes: For 'half past' use han, as in sanji han; hanbun ni suru = split in half.

example.ja: 残りは明日やる。

examplePolite.romaji: Nokori wa ashita yarimasu.
examplePolite.ja: 残りは明日やります。
examplePolite.english: I'll do the rest tomorrow.

notes: From nokoru (be left over). Leftover food is nokorimono.

use: A part of a group or whole, often 'some people': ichibu no hito.

example.ja: 一部の人しか知らない。

examplePolite.romaji: Ichibu no hito shika shirimasen.
examplePolite.ja: 一部の人しか知りません。
examplePolite.english: Only some people know.

notes: Also 'one copy' of a document or magazine.

example.ja: この部分がよくわからない。
example.english: I don't really get this part.

examplePolite.romaji: Kono bubun ga yoku wakarimasen.
examplePolite.ja: この部分がよくわかりません。
examplePolite.english: I don't quite understand this part.

notes: A specific part you can point at; ichibu is 'some of' a whole.

use: The usual word for a song you listen to or play.

example.ja: この曲、好きなんだ。

examplePolite.romaji: Kono kyoku, suki nan desu.
examplePolite.ja: この曲、好きなんです。
examplePolite.english: I really like this song.

notes: Uta is the song as sung, with words. Also counts songs: sankyoku = three songs.

example.ja: 来週、ライブ行くんだ。
example.english: I'm going to a gig next week.

examplePolite.romaji: Raishuu, raibu ni iku n desu.
examplePolite.ja: 来週、ライブに行くんです。
examplePolite.english: I'm going to a concert next week.

notes: Used for any pop or rock show, big or small; konsaato sounds more formal or classical.

use: Usually a private room you rent by the hour with friends.

example.ja: 今日カラオケ行かない？
example.english: Want to go to karaoke today?

examplePolite.romaji: Kyou karaoke ni ikimasen ka?
examplePolite.ja: 今日カラオケに行きませんか？
examplePolite.english: Would you like to go to karaoke today?

notes: Said ka-ra-o-ke, four even beats, not 'carry-oh-key'.

example.ja: なんかスポーツやってる？

examplePolite.romaji: Nanika supootsu o yatte imasu ka?
examplePolite.ja: 何かスポーツをやっていますか？
examplePolite.english: Do you do any sports?

notes: You yaru or suru a sport; asobu is for playing around.

example.ja: 昨日野球見に行った。
example.english: I went to see a baseball game yesterday.

examplePolite.romaji: Kinou yakyuu o mi ni ikimashita.
examplePolite.ja: 昨日野球を見に行きました。
examplePolite.english: I went to watch baseball yesterday.

notes: Japan's most-watched sport; a game is shiai.

example.ja: 仕事のあとジム行く。
example.english: I'm going to the gym after work.

examplePolite.romaji: Shigoto no ato, jimu ni ikimasu.
examplePolite.ja: 仕事のあと、ジムに行きます。
examplePolite.english: I go to the gym after work.

notes: A fitness gym; a school sports hall is taiikukan.
